NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on the BJP over law and order in West Bengal, claiming that more than 2,400 rape cases were recorded in the state in just five months.In a post on X, the All India Trinamool Congress cited figures attributed to the State Crime Records Bureau and claimed that 2,454 rape cases were registered during the five-month period.The party also cited figures for other crimes, claiming that Bengal recorded 600 murder cases, 13,114 attempted murder cases and 32,341 cases of assault causing grievous hurt during the same period.“2,400+ RAPE CASES IN BENGAL IN JUST 5 MONTHS UNDER BJP!” the TMC said in its post, accusing the BJP of turning Bengal into a place where women and ordinary citizens are increasingly being forced to live in fear.The party questioned the BJP's claim of ensuring a “safe and secure Bengal”, asking whether the crime figures reflected the reality behind its promises.“Is this the ‘safe and secure Bengal’ BJP promised?” the TMC asked, referring to the BJP's “Bhorsha In, Bhoy Out” slogan.The party said the people of Bengal deserved “security, accountability and justice” rather than what it called “jumlas”.The TMC also directly targeted CM Suvendu Adhikari, accusing him of hiding behind “slogans and hollow promises” and alleging that he had failed the people of Bengal.“YOU have failed the people of Bengal,” the party said, adding that it had been raising the issue since the beginning and that the alleged failures of the BJP were becoming harder to hide.
Article Summary: The All India Trinamool Congress claims 2,454 rape cases were registered during the five-month period. The party also cited figures for other crimes, claiming that Bengal recorded 600 murder cases, 13,114 attempted murder cases and 32,341 cases of assault causing grievous hurt.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have received a complaint from Akashvani staffers against Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, as well as the MPs and others accompanying them, for allegedly forcing their way into the Akashvani office.Rahul and Priyanka were briefly detained on Tuesday night after an over eight-hour sit-in at the Akashvani Bhawan premises. The protest began after police stopped INDIA bloc MPs from marching towards the Election Commission's office, around 300 metres away, over allegations of "vote chori".Rahul had entered the All India Radio premises on Parliament Street around noon and joined the protest.Earlier, during the march from Parliament towards the EC headquarters, he climbed atop barricades as opposition MPs raised slogans of "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod". Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule and several other opposition leaders also took part in the march.Security personnel stopped the MPs near the NITI Aayog office amid heavy barricading around Parliament and the EC office.Police later forcibly removed Rahul and several other Congress leaders and MPs, including K C Venugopal, Charanjit Singh Channi, Pawan Khera, K Suresh, Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, Deepender Hooda, Praniti Shinde, Varsha Gaekwad and Imran Pratapgarhi, as the protesting MPs and leaders were cleared from the AIR premises.The detainees were taken to New Police Lines at Kingsway Camp. Police said around 250 people, including 50 MPs, were detained on Tuesday night following the prolonged sit-in. Gandhi and other Congress leaders were released around 10 pm, the party said.The opposition MPs were protesting over "vote chori" allegations and seeking the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar in the wake of media reports alleging differences within the Election Commission over the SIR of electoral rolls and other issues.
Article Summary: Rahul and Priyanka were briefly detained on Tuesday night after an over eight- hour sit-in at the Akashvani Bhawan premises. Rahul had entered the All India Radio premises on Parliament Street around noon and joined the protest.

Article Title: ‘This is merely the beginning’: Congress warns Gyanesh Kumar after INDIA bloc protest

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Pawan Khera on Tuesday warned the government that the INDIA bloc’s protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was only the beginning, shortly after opposition MPs were released from New Police Lines in Kingsway Camp.“The words being spoken today are going to cost them dearly. The people of this country know exactly how to deal with such words and the people who utter them,” Khera told reporters after his release. He said those in power should “mend their ways right now” and warned that the public would “bring down those who are currently riding the high horse of arrogance”.Khera named Prime Minister Narendra Modi, CEC Gyanesh Kumar, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Union home minister Amit Shah, saying they “will not sleep tonight—nor will they sleep soundly ever again—because they have betrayed the nation”.“If Gyanesh Kumar thinks that just because we went home today, it is all over, he needs to understand that this is merely the beginning—nothing has ended yet,” Khera said.Earlier on Tuesday, Delhi Police detained Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi along with several other Congress MPs from near Akashvani Bhavan following a day-long protest demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The INDIA bloc MPs had marched from the Parliament complex towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission headquarters, seeking a meeting with the election commissioners over their allegations of “vote chori”.Police stopped the march near Akashvani Bhavan, following which the MPs staged a sit-in.After nearly nine hours of protest, police moved in and detained several opposition MPs, including Khera, KC Venugopal and Amrinder Singh Raja Warring. Around 50 MPs were detained and taken to New Police Lines at Kingsway Camp, according to PTI, citing sources.“The Election Commission office is barely 50 metres away, but we were not allowed to go there. I do not understand what the problem is. The Election Commission's job is to conduct elections properly. At least 300 MPs want to meet Gyanesh Kumar. But he is scared. I don't know what's happening in the country,” Rahul said.“If the representatives of the people cannot meet the Election Commission, then what is the meaning of democracy?” he said.

Article Title: CBI raids CM Bhagwant Mann’s camp office, his OSD’s home in graft probe
Article Text:
Central forces stand guard as CBI searches Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann's camp office in Chandigarh

After CBI raid in graft probe, Punjab CM claims BJP has started poll preparation

NEW DELHI/CHANDIGARH: CBI registered an FIR against Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann’s OSD Rajbir Ghuman and five others Tuesday, following it up with raids on eight locations, including the CM’s camp office in Chandigarh.The coordinated search came within hours of the state govt moving Supreme Court against Punjab and Haryana high court’s order for a CBI probe into ED’s allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through the OSD.The search at Mann’s camp office in House No 50 of Sector 2 started around 6pm, sending shockwaves through the administration. It was at this office that Ghuman used to allegedly meet the co-accused, said CBI sources. A CBI team also visited Ghuman’s home in his village, Gharachon in Sangrur.CBI said the case was registered following a court order that was based on an ED report. The investigation centres on allegations of corruption and abuse of power and political influence. Apart from Ghuman, those named by CBI in the FIR are Nitin Gohal, Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder, RS Nagra and “unknown public servant(s) and private person(s)”.Nitin is alleged to be a “liaison” in the “cash-for-transfer” scandal with access to Ghuman. His brother Jitin was allegedly provided access to CMO through Ghuman and Dr Romi Mahajan, described as an “associate” who allegedly worked with Ghuman and helped coordinate appointments. Devinder is an AAP youth activist and Nagra is a “private associate”.CBI searched premises linked to the accused in Chandigarh, Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, Sangrur and Jalandhar and seized laptops, mobile phones and financial documents.The seized laptops, mobile phones and documents are currently undergoing forensic scrutiny to establish evidence of bribery, official impropriety, and financial paper trails.Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann responded through a post on X in Punjabi, “BJP has started preparations for Punjab elections. A CBI raid was conducted at my camp office. Now ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab so that Punjab govt and I can be defamed. BJP is in panic as it sees the love received from people.”CBI said the FIR is meant to investigate allegations of corruption against OSD to CM, Rajbir Ghuman, and his associates for “influencing and manipulating postings of officers, including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land-related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits”.“It is also alleged that the accused public servants purportedly accessed and provided drafts of orders and policies to private persons prior to their issuance by the govt,” said CBI, adding that those named in the FIR include two public servants, middlemen, and associates.ED had conducted searches in Punjab from May 7-10 in a PMLA case and written to the DGP on July 30 to register a case.Advocate Nikhil Saraf filed a PIL in HC, alleging ED had written three letters to the Punjab DGP, seeking registration of an FIR against Ghuman and others, yet Punjab Police didn’t do so.On Monday, a division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor heard the PIL and said, “We are not impressed by the manner in which Punjab Police has acted so far and, therefore, deem it appropriate to entrust investigation to CBI.”
Article Summary: CBI searches premises linked to the accused in Chandigarh, Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, Sangrur and Jalandhar. The seized laptops, mobile phones and documents are currently undergoing forensic scrutiny to establish evidence of bribery and official impropriety.

NEW DELHI: Opposition parties on Wednesday sought an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu to raise issues related to chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, sources told news agency ANI.The move came a day after INDIA bloc leaders held a protest against the Election Commission and the CEC over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Meanwhile, Congress chief and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge has invited opposition MPs for lunch at 1pm in Delhi.During the meeting, the MPs are expected to sign a letter seeking an appointment with CEC Gyanesh Kumar, as news agency ANI quoted sources.The INDIA bloc has been demanding answers from the Election Commission on SIR and has accused the poll panel of not addressing its concerns. The protest was part of the opposition's wider “Save Democracy” campaign.On Tuesday, leaders of several INDIA bloc parties marched towards Nirvachan Sadan but were stopped by barricades.The leaders then staged a sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan. During the protest, Rahul Gandhi claimed that around 300 Opposition MPs wanted to meet the election commissioners and submit their concerns.Several opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, were later detained by Delhi Police.Rahul Gandhi defended the protest, saying the opposition only wanted to meet the election commissioners and raise questions about the revision of electoral rolls.After the protest, the Election Commission said no political party had sought an appointment with the poll panel until 4pm.In a statement, the EC said Delhi Police informed it around 4pm that a delegation of around 240 MPs, led by Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, wanted to meet the election commissioners and submit a memorandum at the Parliament House Annexe.The poll panel said the proposed venue and the way the meeting was sought were “unusual” given its established protocol.The Election Commission said it later considered sending its most senior executive officer to receive the memorandum from the opposition MPs at the venue. However, the offer was rejected.
Article Summary: Opposition parties on Wednesday sought an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu. The move came a day after INDIA bloc leaders held a protest against the Election Commission and the CEC. Article Title: 80% vote in West Bengal bypolls amid rigging, intimidation charges
Article Text:
AJUP chief Humayun Kabir was detained for allegedly provoking tension

KOLKATA/CHENNAI/GUWAHATI: Bypolls across three states and one Union territory saw high but uneven turnouts Tuesday, with Bengal's Nandigram and Rejinagar recording 80% turnout amid allegations of rigging, voter intimidation and police interference, while polling in one Puducherry and two Tamil Nadu assembly seats and Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency remained largely peaceful.Nandigram recorded above 80% turnout by 7pm, but voters reported being turned away from booths. CM Suvendu Adhikari, who had vacated the seat after winning both Nandigram and Bhowanipore in May, said: "In 2016, I won by 82,000 votes, my highest margin ever. I believe that record will be broken this time."Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, out on bail following his arrest in a 2007 case after he filed his nomination, said the election had been "looted" and complained of blocked agents, voters being denied entry, assault and vandalism. CPI and ISF candidate Sabe Mirza Khan also alleged rigging.Rejinagar recorded 80% turnout, with allegations of police interference dominating polling. AJUP chief Humayun Kabir, who gave up Rejinagar and kept Nowda after winning both in May, was detained after police accused him of provoking tension. Videos showed police grabbing Kabir by his shirt and taking him away. He was released after 12 hours. His son Golam Nabi Azad is the AJUP candidate.Congress and TMC alleged widespread rigging and removal of polling agents. BJP's Shankharavh Sarkar clashed with central forces after being asked to move away from voters.Tamil Nadu saw a turnout dip from April's elections. Madurantakam recorded 86%, down from 93%, while Dharapuram saw 80%, against 89% in April. Both saw three-way contests involving TVK, DMK and AIADMK.Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha bypolls recorded 76% turnout. BJP's Devasish Sharma, Congress's Sibamoni Bora and AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal are the main contenders among 15 candidates.Puducherry's Thattanchavady recorded 78% turnout by 5pm, with final figures expected to rise. The contest is seen as a test for the four-month-old NDA govt led by CM N Rangasamy, whose resignation from the seat necessitated the bypolls. Counting is scheduled for October 9.
Article Summary: Bengal's Nandigram and Rejinagar recorded 80% turnout amid allegations of rigging, voter intimidation and police interference. Polling in one Puducherry and two Tamil Nadu assembly seats and Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency remained largely peaceful.

Article Title: Election Commission: Was ready to meet 240 opposition MPs but not at their chosen venue
Article Text:
Till 4 pm, no political party had sought an appointment, EC said

NEW DELHI: Election Commission on Tuesday, while willing to meet the 240 opposition party MPs at their request conveyed through Delhi Police, declined to do so at their suggested venue of Parliament House annexe, saying the poll panel's protocol required such meetings to be held only on EC premises and based on a request from the parties' authorised representative."EC considered this request as unusual and therefore, it could not be accepted," the panel said in a statement.As an alternative, EC proposed that its most senior officer on duty could be sent to the meeting venue to receive a memorandum, "which in itself would have been an unprecedented step", said an EC spokesperson. However, this offer was declined by the MPs.While emphasising that any political party may request for a meeting with EC, which would then schedule a date and time, the commission said it must balance its respect for parliamentary and democratic processes with that for its own protocols and conventions, "which are of utmost importance".EC said during the march by certain political parties towards Nirvachan Sadan, "it was learnt through the media that some MPs wished to meet the commission along with their delegation"."It is clarified that, till 4pm, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with EC," the commission said. EC said around 4pm, information was received from police that a delegation of MPs led by Rahul Gandhi wished to meet and submit a memorandum.Referring to the procedure laid down in 2025 for meetings with political parties, EC said if a delegation wishes to meet, it seeks an appointment through its authorised representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides. "This is a regular practice," EC said.When the panel was considering the proposal, it was informed by the Delhi Police DCP that the meeting was sought to be held with 240 MPs and the proposed venue was the Parliament House annexe, it said. "EC, considering its protocol to meet political parties only on its own premises and its procedure to only schedule such meetings in consultation with the parties' authorised representative, declined the offer," it said.
Article Summary: Election Commission was willing to meet the 240 opposition party MPs at their request conveyed through Delhi Police. But it declined to do so at their suggested venue of Parliament House annexe. The poll panel's protocol required such meetings to be held only on EC premises and based on a request from the parties' authorised representative.

Article Title: 'Unusual request': EC explains why it could not meet Rahul Gandhi-led opposition MPs
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Amid the onging row with opposition parties over SIR, the Election Commission of India on Tuesday said that no political party had formally sought an appointment to meet."Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to today's developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission," said the EC in a statement.The EC added that it found out through Delhi Police that "a delegation of MPs, led by the Hon'ble leader of the opposition, Shri Rahul Gandhi , wished to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum."Further clarifying the rules and justifying itself, the EC cited procedures laid down for meetings with political parties. "All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly Authorised Representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides," it said.The EC further claimed that after 4 PM, while it was considering the proposed meeting, the Delhi Police informed it that the delegation comprised 240 MPs and that they wanted to meet at the Parliament House Annexe.The Commission termed the request “unusual” and said it could not be accepted because, under ECI protocol, meetings with political parties are held only at the Commission’s premises.The poll panel said it then offered to send its senior-most officer on duty to the Parliament House Annexe to receive the MPs’ memorandum. The EC described this as “an unprecedented step”, but said the offer was also declined by the MPs.The Commission said it respected “the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country”, while stressing that its own protocols and conventions were also important. It reiterated that political parties can request meetings with the EC at any time, after which the Commission schedules a date and time depending on its availability.This came as INDIA bloc leaders staged a massive march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding a meeting with the poll panel over their allegations of “vote chori” and seeking the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined the sit-in near Akashvani Bhavan, but police later cleared the protest site and detained several opposition MPs.Read more: Rahul and Priyanka removed from protest site after high drama - watch
Article Summary: The Election Commission of India on Tuesday said that no political party had formally sought an appointment to meet. NEW DELHI: An FIR has been registered against a BJP Booth Level Agent (BLA) for allegedly filing "false" Form-7 applications seeking the deletion of 30 voters from the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR).The case is the first FIR registered in Telangana over allegations of submitting Form-7 applications containing "false" information, news agency PTI reported.The FIR was registered at Chikkadapally Police Station against BJP BLA S Balachander following a complaint by an election official. Police have invoked relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Representation of the People Act."Following a complaint that the BLA submitted forms for deletion of 30 electors, we have registered an FIR. The matter is under investigation," a police official told PTI.Earlier, Telangana Congress leaders had approached Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharshan Reddy, alleging that Balachander, the BJP's BLA in Musheerabad, had submitted Form-7 applications seeking deletion of the names of 30 electors.The Congress alleged that the applications amounted to an attempt to unlawfully remove genuine voters from the electoral rolls and sought legal action against those responsible.The Telangana Congress also approached Hyderabad Police Commissioner VC Sajjanar, seeking registration of an FIR and an SIT investigation into what it described as a suspected BJP plan to carry out large-scale deletion of genuine voters during the SIR.In its complaint, the Congress alleged that the BJP BLA in the Musheerabad assembly constituency had submitted Form-7 applications seeking deletion of the names of another BJP BLA, Sharfuddin, and members of his family.Form-7 is used by voters to file objections to the proposed inclusion or seek deletion of a name from an existing electoral roll.The BJP has rejected the allegations. Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao said that no BJP BLA had submitted any such Form-7 applications.Meanwhile, Telangana CEO C Sudharshan Reddy on Monday directed District Election Officers (DEOs) to take action against applicants who knowingly submit false statements or declarations in Form-6, Form-6A, Form-7 and Form-8.In a communication to DEOs, the CEO's office said it had taken note of instances involving bulk Form-7 applications submitted before Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), with allegations that some of these applications were not genuine.
Article Summary: FIR has been registered against a BJP Booth Level Agent (BLA) for allegedly filing "false" Form-7 applications. The applications sought the deletion of 30 voters from the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) Telangana Congress leaders had approached Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharshan Reddy, alleging the applications.

Article Title: 'Once a skunk, always a skunk': DMK questions Rahul Gandhi's stand on Tamil Nadu SIR deletions amid anti-CEC protest

NEW DELHI: Former Congress ally DMK on Tuesday questioned Rahul Gandhi over his stand on SIR-related deletions in Tamil Nadu, even as the Congress MP led an opposition protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi.DMK spokesperson Sarvanan Annadurai called Rahul Gandhi a "skunk" and accused him of being "duplicitous"."What’s the stand of @RahulGandhi with regard to the deletions through SIR in TN? Why is he not endorsing Kharge ji's statement that all state governments elected after SIR should be dissolved?" Once a skunk, always a skunk," the DMK spokesperson added.The DMK snapped ties with the Congress and left the Congress-led INDIA bloc after the party decided to support TVK, which emerged as the single largest party in the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April. TVK governs the state with the support of the Congress, Left parties and the IUML.The DMK, which was voted out of power in Tamil Nadu after a single term, did not attend the INDIA bloc's September 30 meeting in Delhi, where the opposition alliance decided to march to the Election Commission (EC) office on October 6.The INDIA bloc and other groups are demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar after The Indian Express reported last month that the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had lodged at least 14 formal objections over the past 10 months, claiming that the poll body took several decisions, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, without their knowledge.The EC is required to take decisions unanimously or by a 2-1 majority. However, the poll body said disagreements are "normal" in multi-member institutions and that all decisions were ultimately taken unanimously.On Monday, the Supreme Court issued notices to the EC and the Centre on a plea seeking Kumar's suspension and the cancellation of all decisions allegedly taken without the knowledge of Sandhu and Joshi. Article Title: Varanasi woman 'thrashed' after finding husband is HIV+; alleges rape bid by father-in-law
Article Text:
(AI Image) A woman from Varanasi, aged 25, has leveled allegations against her husband and in-laws for concealing his HIV positive status





VARANASI: A woman lodged an FIR with Manduadih police station in Varanasi against her Mau-based husband and in-laws alleging they arranged the marriage in 2024 without disclosing that the groom was HIV positive. When she raised an objection on becoming aware of it after marriage, she was thrashed by them and even tortured for dowry.After a case was lodged under sections 74 (assaulting woman with the intent to outrage her modesty), 77 (watching, capturing or transmitting/disseminating private images or acts of a woman without her consent), 85 (cruelty by husband or his relatives), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 271 (unlawfully or negligently doing an act to spread a life-threatening infection or disease), 318(4) (cheating) and 351(3) (criminal intimidation) of BNS and also a section of the Dowry Prohibition Act on Oct 3, an investigation into this case was started, Manduadih police station in-charge Digambar Upadhyaya said on Tuesday.The 25-year-old woman mentioned in her complaint that after detailed talks between her father and the family of the man and checking the boy’s family background and horoscope, their wedding was finalised in 2024. She claimed that her father had spent Rs 20 lakh on giving gifts, dowry and hosting the wedding ceremony and related rituals.A few months after the wedding, the man’s health began to deteriorate and there was no improvement despite treatment.When the woman tried to know the reason, it became clear that he had already been seeking treatment for HIV infection since before marriage. She alleged that after the truth was exposed, her in-laws started assaulting and threatening her not to disclose the truth to her family.She alleged that her in-laws pressurised her father to pay Rs 5 lakh as dowry and even after Rs 2 lakh was paid, her father-in-law tried to rape her. She alleged that her objectionable videos were also made by her in-laws who threatened to make them viral and kill her. She said she came back to her parental home in Varanasi. She said when her in-laws continued threatening her and her parents, she gave the complaint to Manduadih police on Sept 10, but when no FIR was lodged, she approached senior govt officials, after which her case was registered by police on Oct 3.
Article Summary: A woman from Varanasi, aged 25, has leveled allegations against her husband and in-laws for concealing his HIV positive status. She alleged they arranged the marriage in 2024 without disclosing that the groom was HIV positive. When she raised an objection on becoming aware of it after marriage, she was thrashed by them and even tortured for dowry.

Article Title: Gulzar Singh case: Complainant has no video of father’s death, cops tell Punjab and Haryana high court
Article Text:
The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.





CHANDIGARH: Punjab govt has told the Punjab and Haryana high court that despite repeated efforts, the original video/device on which alleged suicide victim Gulzar Singh’s purported video was recorded has not been handed over to the police by the complainant or his family members.In its status report filed before the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwini Kumar and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the state govt said efforts were made to bring on record the original video/device, but the complainant and the family members of Gulzar Singh did not submit them.The report states that notices under Section 94 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were issued to complainant Lakhwinder Singh, who is Gulzar’s son, on Sept 15, 17, 20 and 27 for the production of the device. The report stated that Lakhwinder, in his statement on Sept 27, stated that he did not have any video regarding the death of his father.The SIT, however, said multiple videos had been collected as part of the investigation through social-media monitoring. “The said videos have been obtained through social monitoring vide DDR No. 45 dated September 26, 2026,” the report states.It states that the videos are being analysed as “there are multiple videos with different versions”.According to the status report, in one of the videos, Gulzar Singh is heard naming Raj Sarpanch, Vicky, Sukha Conductor and Gona, who are accused in the present FIR. The report states that “his statement in the said video corroborates with the statement given by complainant Lakhwinder Singh”.The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.The police said notices were also issued under Section 94 of the BNSS to media channels, calling upon them to provide the original video recordings along with requisite certificates under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, “for the purpose of establishing their authenticity”.The status report has been filed by Sangrur senior superintendent of police Dr Rajvot Grewal, a member of the special investigation team that is probing the suicide case, in compliance with the high court’s Sept 16 order.The report states that FIR No. 204 dated Sept 8 was registered at Dirba police station under Section 108 of the BNS and sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against five persons — Baljit Singh alias Raj, Sukhdev Singh alias Sukha Conductor, Vicky Singh alias Vicky Member, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur.It states that Baljit, Vicky, Gona and Baljinder were arrested on Sept 8 and remanded in judicial custody. Sukhdev, however, “is absconding as on today”.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the local drug menace on Sept 6.The SIT said a look-out circular was issued against Sukhdev, besides a message to all SHOs in Punjab, a public notice and letters to the Regional Transport Authority, Lead Bank, Sangrur, and Bureau of Immigration to trace him and gather information about his vehicle, financial transactions and travel history. Multiple raids were also conducted at his residence, relatives houses and other possible locations.A petition was filed before the Punjab and Haryana high court seeking transfer of the investigation to the CBI or another independent agency, alleging that Gulzar Singh had faced intimidation and that his video statement contained allegations against certain persons.
Article Summary: Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema.

Article Title: A day after high-voltage protest, Mallikarjun Kharge to host INDIA bloc MPs’ lunch at Delhi's Sagar Ratna
Article Text:
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge will host the INDIA bloc MPs for lunch at Sagar Ratna.





NEW DELHI: A day after INDIA bloc MPs staged a march and Rahul Gandhi led an over eight-hour sit-in over the Opposition's "vote chori" allegations, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge will host MPs of the alliance for lunch at a Delhi restaurant on Wednesday.The lunch is scheduled for 1.30pm at Sagar Ratna on Janpath, sources said. The meeting is expected to provide the Opposition another opportunity to discuss its next steps over the "vote chori" issue and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The lunch comes a day after a dramatic day of protests in the national capital, during which Parliament Street was effectively shut down as Opposition MPs attempted to march towards the Election Commission's office.Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, led the protest and later staged a sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan after police stopped the MPs from proceeding towards the Election Commission.The sit-in, which began around noon, continued for more than eight hours and ended after 8pm when police personnel forcibly removed Gandhi and other protesters and took them into custody.Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Congress leader K C Venugopal, TMC's Derek O'Brien and other Opposition MPs were among those detained.Police said around 250 people were detained during the protests.Most of the detained leaders were released after a brief detention, while Gandhi and other MPs were released after 10pm following around two hours in custody.The protests began around 11am on Tuesday when Opposition MPs marched from Parliament House towards the Election Commission amid heavy police barricading.Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and several Congress MPs later entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises, around 200 metres from the Election Commission's office, and demanded permission to meet the election commissioners.The day ended with clashes and jostling between protesters and police as officers moved to clear the site.Against this backdrop, Wednesday's lunch hosted by Kharge is likely to be closely watched for indications of the Opposition's next course of action on the "vote chori" issue and its demand for action against the CEC.
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge will host MPs of the alliance for lunch at a Delhi restaurant on Wednesday. Lunch is scheduled for 1.30pm at Sagar Ratna on Janpath, sources said. Meeting is expected to provide the Opposition another opportunity to discuss its next steps over the "vote chori" issue.

Article Title: '908 out of 909 deleted': CJP's Saurav Das alleges mass disenfranchisement under SIR in Delhi, shares video
Article Text:
CJP spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that 908 out of 909 voters in Bela Estate were deleted in Delhi





NEW DELHI: "What Gyanu has actually done nationwide," CJP spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that the Election Commission under CEC Gyanesh Kumar had deleted the names of 908 out of 909 voters in the Bela Estate settlement in Delhi’s Chandni Chowk constituency during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).Saurav Das posted on X, "See how Gyanesh Kumar’s Election Commission ensured that only ONE out of 909 persons in this Delhi settlement survive the SIR.""This is the Bela Estate settlement in Delhi’s Chandni Chowk constituency where 908 out of 909 voters have been deleted during the SIR in Delhi." Das said."This is only a small sample of what Gyanu has actually done NATIONWIDE, against the people of India, all in the service of ONE political party," he added."13+ crore voters have been deleted from the voters list across India. 98 crore eligible voters existed in 2024. The biggest disenfranchisement exercise in the world, under Gyanu, at the behest of Modi and Shah!," Das said.'Now these people and the young generation will ensure Gyanu’s accountability starting October 10th," Das said.Earlier CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke accused the BJP-led central government of using the SIR exercise to undermine voting rights and alleged that the Maharashtra Police were trying to prevent CJP activists from attending the party’s proposed October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar.At a press conference on Tuesday, Dipke said, "One Nation, One Election is just a slogan. The actual intention of the ruling dispensation is to push the country toward 'one nation, one political party'."Alleging that the "true objective" behind one nation, one election was to "snatch away the voting rights guaranteed to citizens by Dr B R Ambedkar," Dipke said "this is not about one party or ideology, it is a fight for the survival of Indian democracy."He had also accused Chandrapur police of serving notices to CJP workers and asking them not to attend the October 10 protest."I have said multiple times that the Maharashtra Police is the best police force in the country, and the Delhi Police should learn from them. But it is heart-breaking that the Chandrapur police served notices to CJP workers, asking them not to participate in the protest at Jantar Mantar. They also asked CJP workers about the source of funds for travelling to Jantar Mantar," he said."The police stated (in the notice) that the agitation is going to be "violent". How do the police know so early that the agitation would be violent? Have they planned anything in advance?'' he asked.Dipke also targeted Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis over the alleged police action.''Why Devendra Fadnavis is trying to be UP CM Yogi Adityanath 2.0? He should know about the legacy of Maharashtra. He should not disrespect and misuse the Maharashtra Police for political ambitions. Instead of harassing our workers, they should arrest me...If they want they should put me behind the bars and charge me with UAPA, NSA. They should not harass our workers,'' he said.Dipke had said the CJP would continue its agitation and reiterated that the entire country would become Jantar Mantar if Gyanesh Kumar was not removed as CEC."We have three demands. First is the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, along with that, he should be booked under criminal charges and the SIR should be stopped. The last demand is that the appointment of Election Commissioner should be done independently and neutrally," Dipke said, adding that the EC should not be merely the "choice of Amit Shah and Narendra Modi.''
Article Summary: Saurav Das posted on X, "See how Gyanesh Kumar’s Election Commission ensured that only ONE out of 909 persons in this Delhi settlement survive the SIR" CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke accused the BJP-led central government of using the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise to undermine voting rights. Dipke had also accused Chandrapur police of serving notices to CJP workers and asking them not to attend the October 10 protest.

Article Title: 'Fadnavis, why are you trying to become Yogi Adityanath': Abhijeet Dipke questions Chandrapur cops’ notices to Delhi-bound members

Article Title: Kolhapur tutor kidnapped from Latur home, murdered in Beed over suspicion of affair, four arrested
Article Text:
File photo :

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A 32-year-old tutor was allegedly called out of his home in Latur, abducted and taken to a stone-crushing centre in neighbouring Beed district, where four men beat him to death on suspicion that he was having an affair with a woman, police said.One of the accused later took the unconscious victim, Madhav alias Nitin Dhanaji Sangme, to Govt Medical College and Hospital in Latur. He allegedly told doctors that Sangme had been found injured near Bardapur. Doctors declared Sangme dead.Police at the hospital became suspicious of the account. They questioned the accused, and the alleged abduction and assault came to light.Sangme worked as a tutor with a private coaching class in Kolhapur. He had returned to his home in Latur for preparations for his brother’s engagement.Police said Sangme was called to Vitthal-Rukmini temple area near Kanheri Chowk on Sunday afternoon. Four men allegedly bundled him into a car and drove him to a stone-crushing centre at Bardapur in Beed district’s Ambajogai taluka.Latur SP Amol Tambe said the accused suspected Sangme of having an affair with a woman.“The victim was assaulted with iron rods, belts and sticks. The investigation is underway to establish the exact circumstances leading to the murder ,” Tambe said.Police identified the accused as Prithviraj Deshmukh, Dhawal Deshmukh, Prathamesh Reddy and Aditya Bhalke, all residents of Latur.The four allegedly assaulted Sangme until he lost consciousness. Bhalke then took him to the Latur hospital and claimed that he had found Sangme injured near Bardapur, police said.Shivajinagar police personnel at the hospital questioned Bhalke after becoming suspicious of his version. The alleged abduction and assault emerged during questioning.Inspector Santosh Patil, who is investigating the case, said police were verifying the sequence of events and the role of each accused. “We have registered a case of abduction and murder and are investigating the motive,” Patil said.Shivajinagar police registered the case on a complaint lodged by Sangme’s younger brother Narendra.The four accused were produced before a court on Tuesday and remanded in police custody for four days. Police are now collecting evidence linked to the murder.
Article Summary: Madhav alias Nitin Dhanaji Sangme, 32, was abducted from his home in Latur. Four men allegedly bundled him into a car and drove him to a stone-crushing centre at Bardapur in Beed district’s Ambajogai taluka. The four allegedly assaulted Sangme until he lost consciousness.

They should maintain their self-respect and not act like Delhi Police,” he said.Dipke said notices had been issued to his colleagues in Maharashtra and Rajasthan.“Instead of harassing my colleagues, arrest me. I am sitting here. Apply whatever laws you want against me, but do not trouble my colleagues,” he said.Dipke alleged growing anger among students over examination-related issues and demanded action against those responsible for cancelling examinations. He also raised the alleged assault on tribal student activist Rahul in Nandurbar and asked why activists fighting for tribal students were being targeted.He also criticised governor Jishnu Dev Varma , calling him a “puppet” of the govt and alleging that technical issues were being used to delay action.Dipke, while alleging irregularities concerning electoral rolls and Form 6, demanded resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. “They ask us whether we took permission for the agitation. Gyanesh Kumar should first explain whether he took permission before cancelling 13 crore votes,” he said.Dipke also questioned the govt’s handling of the Election Commission’s clarification and alleged that special treatment was being given to Fadnavis. He also warned that any coercive action against the protesters could lead to a nationwide agitation.
Article Summary: Abhijeet Dipke questioned the Chandrapur police for issuing notices to members of his organisation to participate in a proposed protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. He also criticised chief minister Devendra Fadnavis over the issue. “Why are you trying to become Yogi Adityanath? This is Maharashtra,” he said.

Article Title: ‘Why is Fadnavis trying to be Yogi Adityanath 2.0?’: Abhijeet Dipke attacks Maharashtra govt
Article Text:
Abhijeet Dipke, founder of Cockroach Janta Party, criticized the BJP government for its 'One Nation, One Election' initiative





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday criticised the BJP-led central government, alleging that the real objective behind 'One Nation, One Election' was "one nation, one political party".He also accused the Maharashtra Police of harassing CJP activists and questioned why chief minister Devendra Fadnavis was trying to be "Yogi Adityanath 2.0", news agency PTI reported.Ahead of the party's proposed fresh agitation at Jantar Mantar on October 10, Dipke alleged that police in Maharashtra's Chandrapur district had issued notices to CJP activists, pressuring them not to attend the planned protest demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise and the functioning of the poll body.Addressing a press conference, Dipke said, "One Nation, One Election is just a slogan. The actual intention of the ruling dispensation is to push the country toward 'one nation, one political party'."Alleging that the "true objective" behind one nation, one election was to "snatch away the voting rights guaranteed to citizens by Dr BR Ambedkar", Dipke said, "this is not about one party or ideology; it is a fight for the survival of Indian democracy.""I have said multiple times that the Maharashtra Police is the best police force in the country, and the Delhi Police should learn from them. But it is heart-breaking that the Chandrapur police served notices to CJP workers, asking them not to participate in the protest at Jantar Mantar. They also asked CJP workers about the source of funds for travelling to Jantar Mantar," he said."The police stated (in the notice) that the agitation is going to be 'violent'. How do the police know so early that the agitation would be violent? Have they planned anything in advance?" he asked."Why is the Maharashtra Police behaving like Delhi Police? What do they have to do if a person is going to Delhi from Chandrapur?" he said.Targeting Fadnavis, Dipke said the chief minister should be aware of Maharashtra's legacy, PTI reported."Why is Devendra Fadnavis trying to be UP CM Yogi Adityanath 2.0? He should know about the legacy of Maharashtra. He should not disrespect and misuse the Maharashtra Police for political ambitions. Instead of harassing our workers, they should arrest me. If they want, they should put me behind bars and charge me with UAPA, NSA. They should not harass our workers," he said.Dipke said he had come across two notices issued by police in Chandrapur district and claimed that similar notices were also issued in Rajasthan by the local CID to a person named Mukesh, warning him of legal action if he attended the October 10 protest.He also criticised directions to CJP activists against posting anything on social media that could lead to violence. "We speak about (Mahatma) Gandhi and B R Ambedkar. Do they think it is violent?" he asked.Dipke also alleged that Rahul Pawara, who is leading a protest of tribal students in Maharashtra, was facing police harassment, PTI reported."Yesterday, the Adivasi students led by Rahul Pawara faced repression in Mumbai and some students were beaten up. If the son of Ambani or an MP or MLA was protesting, would the police behave in such a manner?" he asked, adding that Pawara was fighting to secure good education for tribal students.Dipke said Maharashtra Police were once compared to Scotland Yard because of their efficiency and should maintain that image.Referring to an ACP of Delhi Police who has faced accusations of harassing women journalists, Dipke claimed that the officer was promoted "as a reward" and asked if the Maharashtra Police wanted such a "benchmark".On the ongoing agitation by Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) aspirants, Dipke said they were demanding leak-proof examinations, accountability and removal of those responsible for paper leaks, and that the government should understand their anger, PTI reported.He also questioned Vivek Bhimanwar's past appointment as MPSC chairman by the Governor."Why did the Governor appoint the Chief Minister's friend as Chairman of MPSC? I am very sorry to say this, but in this era, the Governor is merely a puppet of those who are sitting in the government," Dipke said.He reiterated that the entire country would become Jantar Mantar if Gyanesh Kumar was not removed as CEC."We have three demands. First is the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar; along with that, he should be booked under criminal charges and the SIR should be stopped. The last demand is that the appointment of the Election Commissioner should be done independently and neutrally," Dipke said, adding that the EC should not be merely the "choice of Amit Shah and Narendra Modi."(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of Cockroach Janta Party, criticized the BJP government for its 'One Nation, One Election' initiative. He also accused the Maharashtra Police of harassing CJP activists and questioned why chief minister Devendra Fadnavis was trying to be "Yogi Adityanath 2.0"

Article Title: Mahayuti to fight Gokul dairy election collectively, Fadnavis leaves lead role to Mushrif
Article Text:
Kolhapur

Gokul Election In A Nutshell





: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has said there will be no intervention at his level in the election for Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul dairy, and NCP leader and minister Hasan Mushrif is taking the lead on behalf of Mahayuti.Fadnavis’s remarks have come amid talks to hold the election unopposed, ceding some seats to the panel led by Congress MLC Satej Patil to avoid an election amid the ongoing drought crisis. “Mahayuti partners will contest Gokul election in alliance. At present, Gokul dairy is led by Hasan Mushrif and he is also taking lead for the election. The leaders of Mahayuti’s partners be it Chandrakant Patil, Mahadik’s, Prakash Abitkar, Rajesh Kshirsagar and their supporters will work together. Gokul dairy’s election is local and limited to cooperative sector. Therefore, at my level, there will be no intervention,” said Fadnavis.Thursday, Oct 8, is the last day for the withdrawal of the nomination, while the final list of the candidates will be released and the distribution of the symbols carried out on Friday. There are 25 posts of directors for Gokul dairy election. The dairy, which supplies milk to Mumbai, Pune and Goa, has a total turnover of around Rs 3,000 crore and is connected to most of the rural households in Kolhapur district, and is therefore politically sensitive.The seat-sharing within Mahayuti has been stuck. Mushrif wants a larger share for his party, while BJP wants no less than what Mushrif will get.Meanwhile, Satej Patil, Congress MLC, has declared that come what may, there will be no unopposed election for Gokul. “Rumours are being spread about making the election uncontested; this is being done by BJP to corner Mushrif. I am clear on this: we have 25 candidates who have filed nominations, and I am going to announce our panel on Wednesday. If the Mahayuti wants to make the Gokul election unopposed, citing drought conditions, why is it not proposing the same for other ongoing cooperative elections, such as Sangli and Satara district central cooperative banks?” said Patil.Total directors to be elected: 25Total Primary Dairies Eligible To Depute A Delegate To Cast A Vote: 5,423Total Nominations: 240Voting: Oct 18Counting of votes and day of result: Oct 19
Article Summary: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has said there will be no intervention at his level in the election for Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul dairy. NCP leader and minister Hasan Mushrif is taking the lead on behalf of Mahayuti. The dairy supplies milk to Mumbai, Pune and Goa.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: Bawankule directs registration dept to clear 2,316 refund cases in 3-day drive
Article Text:
Chandrashekhar Bawankule

Pune:





Revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule has directed the state registration and stamps department to undertake a three-day special drive from Oct 7 to 9 to clear 2,316 pending cases involving refunds of stamp duty and registration fees across Maharashtra “The drive will reduce the backlog, and eligible citizens will get their refunds faster and in a more transparent and efficient manner,” said deputy Inspector General of Registration (IGR) Rajendra Muthe.The drive will be conducted under Inspector General of Registration and Controller of Stamps Ravindra Binwade and will focus on reducing the backlog pending before stamp district collector offices and expediting quasi-judicial proceedings. The cases include claims where stamp duty or registration fee was paid but the transaction was subsequently cancelled, as well as cases involving excess payment.During the drive, officials will scrutinise pending applications, verify documents, approve or reject claims and prepare treasury dues. Cases requiring higher-level approval will be processed under Section 52-A of the Maharashtra Stamp Act.Joint teams have been constituted for the exercise. For offices in Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Ahilyanagar, Nashik and Nagpur, stamp collectors, officers and staff from other districts have been deputed for two days to assist in clearing the pending cases.
Article Summary: Revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule has directed the state registration and stamps department to undertake a three-day special drive from Oct 7 to 9. The drive will focus on reducing the backlog pending before stamp district collector offices and expediting quasi-judicial proceedings.

Article Title: FIR against Udhayanidhi Stalin for involving child in poll campaign in Dharapuram
Article Text:
Authorities in Dharapuram have filed a case against Udhayanidhi Stalin for infringing on the Model Code of Conduct during a recent election rally





TIRUPUR: Dharapuram Police have registered a case against Tamil Nadu Assembly Opposition Leader Udhayanidhi Stalin for involving a child in an election campaign meeting at Dharapuram, where the Model Code of Conduct is in force for the bypoll.According to a press release issued by Tirupur district police, the incident took place on Saturday near the Periyar statue in Dharapuram town during an election campaign meeting addressed by Udhayanidhi.Police said the Election Commission had clearly instructed political parties and candidates not to involve children in any election-related activities.Police said Udhayanidhi made a child speak at the campaign meeting in a manner that was insulting to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and also used the child for election campaigning.Dharapuram Town Police registered a case against Udhayanidhi. Further investigation is under way, police said.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu Assembly Opposition Leader Udhayanidhi Stalin involved a child in an election campaign meeting at Dharapuram. The Model Code of Conduct is in force for the bypoll. Police said the Election Commission had clearly instructed political parties and candidates not to involve children in election-related activities.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Expelled BJP man seeks anticipatory bail in sexual harassment case
Article Text:
Madurai:





Expelled BJP state general secretary Karuppu M Muruganantham moved Madras high court seeking anticipatory bail in the sexual harassment case filed against him by a woman functionary.The court was hearing the anticipatory bail petition filed by Muruganantham, who apprehends arrest in a case registered against him by the Srirangam all-women police in Trichy district.According to the prosecution, a woman BJP functionary submitted a complaint accusing Muruganantham of sexual exploitation, harassment, repeated threats, and circulating her private images and videos on social media. Based on her complaint, police had registered a case. Following the complaint, Muruganantham was removed from his post in the party.In his petition, Muruganantham stated that he is innocent and has not committed any offence as alleged in the FIR. The woman had lodged a false complaint to damage his reputation. Hence, he sought anticipatory bail.Justice K Murali Shankar posted the case for hearing on October 9.
Article Summary: Karuppu M Muruganantham moved Madras high court seeking anticipatory bail in the sexual harassment case filed against him by a woman functionary. He apprehends arrest in a case registered by the Srirangam all-women police in Trichy district. The woman had lodged a false complaint to damage his reputation.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: Complaint to Keralam CM seeks action against CPM’s Suresh Babu
Article Text:
Former CPM Palakkad district secretary EN Suresh Babu

Thrissur

:





KPCC secretary John Daniel has submitted a complaint to chief minister V D Satheesan seeking action against former CPM Palakkad district secretary E N Suresh Babu, who is facing sexual abuse charges.In his letter to the CM, Daniel alleged that the complaint against Babu, a prominent public figure, raises serious concerns about the safety of women active in public life. He said media reports indicated that, despite receiving the complaint, the CPM brass attempted to hush up the matter as an internal party issue and failed to hand it over to the police.Daniel also demanded action against leader of opposition Pinarayi Vijayan and CPM state secretary M V Govindan for allegedly failing to inform the police even after receiving a complaint of sexual abuse.
Article Summary: KPCC secretary John Daniel has submitted a complaint to chief minister V D Satheesan seeking action against former CPM Palakkad district secretary E N Suresh Babu. Daniel alleged that the complaint against Babu raises serious concerns about the safety of women active in public life.
